Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test intent:
  - testCompareTo_otherEnumType asserts that comparing two different ValuedEnum subclasses (ValuedColorEnum.BLUE vs ValuedLanguageEnum.ENGLISH) must throw ClassCastException.
- Actual implementation examined:
  - ValuedEnum.compareTo(Object other):
    - return iValue - ((ValuedEnum) other).iValue;
  - This method:
    - Blindly casts other to ValuedEnum (which succeeds for any subclass of ValuedEnum, including different enum types).
    - Performs arithmetic on integer values without any type check.
    - Never throws ClassCastException for different enum subclasses.
- Consequence:
  - When comparing ValuedColorEnum to ValuedLanguageEnum, the cast succeeds and the method returns an int (possibly 0 if values match), so no exception is thrown.
  - The test therefore reaches fail() and fails.
- Contrast with base Enum implementation:
  - Enum.compareTo(Object other) checks that other.getClass() == this.getClass(), and if not, either handles same-class-name/different-classloader or throws ClassCastException with a clear message.
  - ValuedEnum.compareTo lacks this type-safety check and thus allows cross-type comparisons.
- Root cause:
  - Missing type compatibility check in ValuedEnum.compareTo allows comparisons across different ValuedEnum subclasses, violating type safety and the expected behavior tested.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
